title: The shepherd
hookLine: he tends sheep for pay, and later says every prophet was a shepherd (Bukhari)

cards: Arak berries, small and dark, picked off the bush by a group of men on the road. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is with them, a grown man now, and he tells them: pick the black ones, they're the best.
Someone asks him a question about that. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the question, and his answer opens a door onto the hills outside Mecca and a young man with a stick and a flock. Today: the shepherd.

teach.h: "IS THERE A PROPHET WHO WAS NOT?"
teach.b: The companions ask: were you a shepherd? And in al-Bukhari's report he answers with a question of his own: is there any prophet who was not? In another report in al-Bukhari, he says it plainly.
Allah sent no prophet who did not tend sheep. And you, they ask? Yes, he says.

teach.h: FOR THE PEOPLE OF MECCA, FOR COINS.
teach.b: I tended them for the people of Mecca, for a few coins. So the orphan from Abu Talib's crowded house earned his keep in the hills, walking slowly behind other people's animals. The Qur'an knows this work.

In surah twenty, Allah asks Musa what is in his right hand, and Musa answers, in Pickthall's words: "This is my staff whereon I lean, and wherewith I beat down branches for my sheep, and wherein I find other uses."
A man about to be sent to Pharaoh, and his first answer is about sheep. Why would shepherding come before prophethood? The hadith doesn't explain, and it's fair to leave that open.
Commentators have offered reasons: sheep are slow and they scatter, and a shepherd learns patience, watchfulness, and how to bring back the one that wanders.
Whatever the reason, the Prophet carried the word into his teaching.

teach.h: EACH OF YOU IS A SHEPHERD.
teach.b: In al-Bukhari he says: each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler, the parent, the worker with someone else's property.
In Arabic, a shepherd is ra'i, and the flock is ra'iyyah, from the same root. Everyone, in that saying, is watching over something.

how: Muslims quote the hadith 'each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock' when speaking of responsibility in families, work and leadership.

one who tends a flock and answers for it

games.q: the Prophet ﷺ tells the companions to pick the black arak berries. they ask: were you a shepherd? what does he answer?
o: no, I learned it in the market.
is there any prophet who was not a shepherd?
I learned it on the caravans to Syria.
games.why: al-Bukhari reports his answer as a question: is there any prophet who did not tend sheep?

practice: Bring to mind something in your keeping that moves at its own pace, a plant, a pet, an old parent, a child learning to read, and match its speed instead of hurrying it in your head.

Watch it the way a shepherd watches a flock, noticing which part is wandering off, and what bringing it back gently would look like. If you pray, you can ask Allah for a shepherd's patience; if not, just stay slow with it.

wordCard.voice: The shepherd. The Prophet tended sheep for the people of Mecca, and said in al-Bukhari that Allah sent no prophet who did not. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: ra'i, shepherd; the flock in the hadith is ra'iyyah, from the same root.
